corrections.text: “Conscious understanding and automatic defensive responses can diverge. Learning involves interacting brain systems; cognitive and behavioral approaches can change responses.”
“Threat processing, bodily responses and conscious fear are related but distinguishable. No single brain region explains the full experience.” Label diagrams conceptual.
“Learning can change responses through several processes. Reconsolidation is one investigated account, with boundary conditions.”

Replace attack table with intervention scope, evidence and limitations. “Evidence-based therapies can develop durable skills and reduce symptoms. The Sovereignty Method is not yet validated as a standalone treatment.”
“Rehearsal should be relevant and manageable. Evaluate what was learned and whether it transfers; intensity alone does not establish benefit.” No mandatory arousal slider target.
“Repeat when it adds useful learning, vary context, and reassess. There is no established universal repetition count for this framework.” Count may log activity, never certify neural updating.
“A field test can assess behavior and transfer. It cannot by itself identify the memory mechanism.” No ‘reconsolidated’ completion state.
Explain inhibitory learning and reconsolidation as distinguishable accounts with overlapping practical questions. Assess durability and return of fear; do not promise erasure.
Replace with educational field guide. No self-administered trauma protocol, clinical efficacy badge or implied equivalent to established therapy.
Distinct personal observations must remain distinct from one another and from measured mechanisms. No private case narrative is published here.
“Some components have research support. The integration, personalization and proposed mechanisms remain open to testing.” Link claim-level evidence.
Correct citation to Nader, Schafe & LeDoux; describe rat fear-memory experiment and protein-synthesis intervention. Do not present it as an imagery trial.
“Expectations can shape anxiety alongside actual circumstances, bodily state, learning history and other factors.” Predictive processing is an explanatory framework.
“Constructionist theories emphasize prediction, concepts and bodily signals. Other accounts emphasize different mechanisms.” Explain predictions and limits, not a winner badge.
“Approach and defensive tendencies may change, but anger, confidence and fear can coexist.” Do not use dominance as the default corrective state.
“Imagery can evoke emotion and share processes with perception; overlap does not make imagined and real events equivalent.”
“Credibility, specificity, context and meaningful feedback may matter; prediction error is not the same quantity as distress.” Keep H-008 open.
Separate factual support, subjective conviction, expected ability and observed performance. A failed test can appropriately lower confidence.
“Sovereignty develops through truthful perception, chosen conduct, recovery and correction; feelings may remain.” Keep no-emotion ideals in philosophical context only.
Retrospective reports have multiple possible explanations and cannot identify a causal mechanism. Detailed personal narratives are withheld.
Optional presentation preferences can be tested; no inferred brain type, clinical matching or diagnosis.
Do not offer a thought-neutralization workflow. Provide conceptual education and condition-specific care context.
Label historical; omit arousal targets and root-cause detector. Use behavior, functioning, adverse effects and uncertainty. Retain 1/4/12-week checks only as proposed checkpoints.
Define metaphors explicitly. Keep spiritual teaching and empirical claims separately navigable and separately tagged.
Threat estimates and perceived coping capacity can both matter. Show them separately; do not calculate an anxiety score or claim a literal neural equation.
Memory updating has boundary conditions. This interface cannot detect a reconsolidation window and provides no timer or universal five-hour prescription.
Imagery and perception can share processes while remaining distinguishable. Motor simulation findings do not demonstrate efficacy of this intervention.

Research examines brain systems involved in learning and regulation. No imaging or physiological study of this protocol establishes repaired temporal tagging, hippocampal restoration, or structural strengthening.
Record intensity descriptively if useful, never as a required target or proof of memory updating. Reassess usefulness, functioning and unwanted effects without escalating to satisfy a number.
Offer text, planning, role-play and optional imagery. These are accessibility choices; their relative benefit in this framework remains to be tested. Omit uncited population percentages.

No breathing, cold-water, forced-arousal or confrontation protocol is prescribed by this educational interface. Ordinary behavioral planning can be offered without claiming autonomic override or guaranteed reciprocal inhibition.
Worsening, no benefit and inconclusive results are valid outcomes. Pause, reassess the premise and consider alternatives; do not assume more repetitions will produce permanent change.
Choose a usable rehearsal format. Whether combining formats improves transfer is an empirical question; more modalities are not automatically better.
Personal reports can generate questions. Evaluating efficacy requires an appropriate prospective design, outcomes, comparison, and reporting of nonresponse and adverse effects.
Separate structural plasticity, subjective experience, useful learning and clinical outcomes.
The recalled quantitative FMT source claim remains unresolved. No numerical efficacy claim is published.
Describe acute symptom regulation, function, relapse and maintenance separately; distinguish SSRIs and benzodiazepines.
Report design-specific findings and uncertainty; do not convert SMD/g to percentage improvement or treat adjunctive results as monotherapy.

takeaways.title: Separate the two questions
takeaways.text: What do I expect will happen? What support or skill could help me respond? Keep these judgments separate rather than calculating an anxiety score.

takeaways.title: Describe a state, not your whole self
takeaways.text: Try “I am noticing anxiety about this conversation.” A feeling can be important without defining your character or deciding your next action.

takeaways.title: Look for ordinary evidence
takeaways.text: Choose a small, safe action that can tell you more about your prediction. Record what happened, including outcomes that did not fit your expectation.
